claim: Phase B3 v17 measurement: running the v15 detector stack (composed: ComplexAssembly + AnnotationClass + PerRule, with iMB155 patches, threshold 0.1) on the full 455-gene Breuer panel at scale=0.05, t_end_s=0.5, seed=42 with both --enable-gene-expression AND --enable-bioelectric (Phase B1 Vmem observable + Phase B2 voltage-gated K+ leak rule active) yields TP=286, FP=3, TN=69, FN=97, MCC=0.5345578057087662. This is BIT-IDENTICAL to the v16 confusion matrix and MCC (TP=286, FP=3, TN=69, FN=97, MCC=0.5345578057087662). The K+ leak rule perturbation did not change a single per-gene prediction. Sweep wall: 5826.93 s (97.1 min) at 4 workers Rust — about 10 percent slower than v16's 5294 s (88 min) due to the additional rule firings. The honest scientific result is that classical bioelectric features at this network density add zero discrimination signal to the v15 detector at single-cell scale; this is consistent with both the synthesis prediction (experiments/quantum_biology_speculation/SYNTHESIS.md) and with the broader Levin-lab framing that bioelectric edge is bigger in multi-cell systems than in isolated cells.
source_detail: Reproducible with: 'python scripts/run_sweep_parallel.py --all --workers 4 --use-rust --scale 0.05 --t-end-s 0.5 --detector composed --seed 42 --threshold 0.1 --enable-imb155-patches --enable-gene-expression --enable-bioelectric --out-dir outputs/phase_b3_v17_full'. Predictions CSV preserved at outputs/phase_b3_v17_full/predictions_parallel_s0.05_t0.5_seed42_thr0.1_w4_composed_gex_bio.csv; metrics JSON at outputs/phase_b3_v17_full/metrics_parallel_s0.05_t0.5_seed42_thr0.1_w4_composed_gex_bio.json. Phase B1 commit 4a8e9bb (bioelectric observable layer) + Phase B2 commit 178b8bc (voltage-gated K+ leak rule) + Phase B3 prep f67596d (sweep flag wiring) + d5e10f6 (gitignore for sweep output dir) all on claude/syn3a-whole-cell-simulator-REjHC. Single-seed measurement.

comparison_to_v16.interpretation: v17 is bit-identical to v16 in confusion matrix and MCC. The K+ leak rule perturbation flowed through the simulator but did not change which genes the v15 detector classifies as essential / nonessential.

comparison_to_v15.flip_direction: TP -> FN (same single flip as v15 -> v16; bioelectric did not introduce or repair any further flips)

wall_comparison_to_v16.interpretation: v17 is ~10 percent slower than v16 because the K+ leak rule fires ~16 tokens per can_fire at resting Vmem ~ -10 mV, contributing ~hundreds of additional events per simulated 0.5 s window. The dynamic perturbation reaches the simulator state but does not propagate to a different detector decision.

caveats: Single-seed measurement (seed=42). v15 was bit-identical across seeds {1, 2, 42}; v16 was single-seed; v17 is single-seed. Whether v17 retains the v15 cross-seed bit-identity property under bioelectric on is not measured here.

v17 = v16 exactly. This is not a noisy null; it's a clean null. The Phase B2 K+ leak rule perturbs ion counts (M_k_c moves by hundreds of ions per 0.5 s window), but the v15 detector's decision surface (annotation-class priors + complex-assembly priors + per-rule silenced-rule decisions) is dominated by features that do NOT depend on K+ count or Vmem. So the perturbation flows through the simulator without affecting predictions. This is informative: it tells us that under the v15 detector at this network density, classical bioelectric features add zero signal.

The bioelectric framework is not refuted by this measurement. Three things would change the picture: (a) a bioelectric-aware detector that explicitly consumes VMEM_MV-derived features (Phase B3 used the v15 detector unmodified, so VMEM_MV in pools is not consumed); (b) a multi-cell setup where bioelectric communication via gap junctions matters (Levin's published work is on multi-cell collective intelligence; Syn3A is single-cell); (c) more aggressive bioelectric dynamics (Phase B2 ships only K+ leak; Na+ / Cl- channels and proton motive force pumping are deferred to Phase B2.5+).

The K+ leak rate constant (100 /s/mV) is a placeholder. A different rate could in principle perturb the simulator more aggressively and either (a) start affecting predictions or (b) destabilize trajectories. The current rate was tuned to give measurable but bounded K+ count drift (~ percent-level over 0.5 s) without runaway. Phase B2.5 / B3 with calibrated rates is future work.
Confidence value 'measured' is correct here: this is a real MCC measurement against a real reference label set (Breuer 2019), reproducible from the predictions CSV, with all flags + seeds documented.

The 10 percent wall slowdown is the cost of the additional K+ leak rule events. Under Rust the cost is dominated by the Python-closure rule's can_fire / apply path (the K+ leak is a closure rule, not a compiled-spec rule). A future Phase B2-vectorize could move it into the compiled propensity vector to recover some of the wall.
